findings.title: The operation matrix omits the resource inputs needed to verify persisted parent and relationship authorization

sourceEvidence.explanation: The operation consumes answerId from route parameters and isAccepted from the body, but its matrix row declares resourceInputs as empty.
The operation consumes answerId and resolves an answer/post relationship, but its matrix row declares resourceInputs as empty.
The operation consumes answerId and isVerified, but its matrix row declares resourceInputs as empty.
The operation consumes postId and resolves a post, but its matrix row declares resourceInputs as empty.
The operation consumes commentId and traverses optional post/answer parents, but its matrix row declares resourceInputs as empty.
The operation consumes postId and answerId and performs separate parent lookups, but its matrix row declares resourceInputs as empty.

findings.impact: The matrix is designated as the operation-level source of truth and the basis for unique future cases. Empty resource-input inventories permit implementation or verification to omit path/body binding, mismatched-parent cases, and foreign course-linked parent cases. This directly weakens the revised requirement that every child resolve through the actual authorized persisted parent.
findings.recommendation: Revise each affected matrix row to enumerate every route, query, and body resource selector and state its required persisted resolution. Include answerId/commentId/postId and mutation-state fields as applicable, plus explicit cases for foreign, deleted, course-linked, and mismatched parents. For comment creation, specify whether exactly one parent is required and, if both identifiers remain accepted, require the answer's post to equal postId.

findings.title: Generic KX rules do not define the distinct authority required by accept, verify, and comment-delete operations

sourceEvidence.explanation: The baseline contract restricts acceptance to the question author, a distinct operation rule not stated in the assigned matrix row.

The baseline uses a staff role check, while the revised KX_MOD policy additionally requires persisted course assignment for course-linked content; the operation row does not identify which parent fields must be selected and checked.

The baseline permits comment author, parent-post author, or staff. The revised generic text says comment deletion requires authorship or explicit moderator authority without deciding whether parent-post authorship remains legitimate authority.

findings.impact: Implementers can reasonably produce incompatible authorization behavior: allowing generic KX authorship to accept answers, omitting course assignment for verification, or removing the existing parent-post-author deletion right. The design therefore does not provide a deterministic authorization contract for these security-sensitive mutations and cannot reliably preserve legitimate normal-role behavior.
findings.recommendation: Add operation-specific rules: acceptance/unacceptance is limited to the actual parent-post author after parent visibility/course authorization; verification requires KX_MOD and, for course-linked posts, actual instructor assignment or eligible ADMIN authority; comment deletion must explicitly decide and encode comment-author, parent-post-author, and moderator rights. Define uniform safe 404 behavior for unauthorized foreign parents before mutation.

implementationRisks.title: Unknown and SUPER_USER role values currently normalize to STUDENT

sourceEvidence.explanation: Every role other than ADMIN or an instructor alias is returned as STUDENT.
The shared guard normalizes the session role and grants eligibility solely from the persisted institute code; it has no explicit SUPER_USER or UNKNOWN denial.

implementationRisks.impact: An active SUPER_USER or unrecognized-role account whose persisted institute is ICS can reach assigned KX operations as a STUDENT instead of receiving the required pre-parse 403. This affects reads, mutations, AI calls, notifications, and gamification effects.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Implement the revised explicit role resolver so SUPER_USER and UNKNOWN remain distinct and fail before protected parsing, reads, writes, or outbound AI calls. Do not use the current default-to-STUDENT normalization at these boundaries.

implementationRisks.title: Current assigned handlers generally check ICS membership but not course-linked parent visibility or assignment/enrollment

sourceEvidence.explanation: The answer lookup selects only post id, authorId, and title; it does not resolve post institute, course, enrollment, or instructor assignment.
Verification resolves the answer and post title but does not enforce course-linked moderator assignment.
Bookmark mutation checks only post existence/deletion and does not enforce institute, course visibility, enrollment, or assignment.
Parent checks cover existence, deletion, and lock status but omit institute and course relationship authorization.

implementationRisks.impact: ICS membership can currently authorize access to foreign, inaccessible, or course-linked KX parents without the persisted relationship required by the revised design.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Implement a shared parent-resolution boundary that constrains KxPost by ICS institute and, when course-linked, by approved enrollment, instructor assignment, or eligible ADMIN authority. Resolve answers and comments through that authorized post before any mutation or private response.

implementationRisks.title: Current staff checks grant institute-wide mutation authority without explicit moderator or course relationship checks

sourceEvidence.explanation: Any normalized ADMIN or INSTRUCTOR passes the staff check after an unscoped answer lookup.
Any normalized ADMIN or INSTRUCTOR can delete the comment without resolving course assignment or an explicit moderator relationship.
The endpoint performs institute-wide analytics reads after KX eligibility alone and has no KX_MOD role check.

implementationRisks.impact: Students may reach private analytics, while instructors can mutate course-linked content outside their assignments. This violates the revised KX_MOD role and persisted-relationship boundary.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Implement explicit KX_MOD authorization before analytics reads and moderator mutations, including canonical instructor aliases, ICS eligibility, and course assignment for course-linked targets. Keep course-less board moderation limited to the explicitly defined ICS moderator roles.

implementationRisks.title: Comment creation can persist two unrelated parents

sourceEvidence.explanation: The handler rejects only when both parent identifiers are absent; it does not reject when both are present.
postId and answerId are validated independently without proving that the answer belongs to the supplied post.
Both identifiers are written to KxComment, allowing unrelated parent references.

implementationRisks.impact: A comment can be attached simultaneously to unrelated post and answer records, making authorization, deletion authority, visibility, and notification semantics ambiguous and enabling cross-resource association.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Require exactly one parent identifier, or atomically resolve answerId through its post and require any supplied postId to match. Apply institute/course visibility authorization to the resolved canonical post before creation.

implementationRisks.title: Answer state mutations and gamification/notification effects are not consistently atomic or idempotent

sourceEvidence.explanation: Acceptance state and notification are transactional, but EXP is awarded afterward and errors are swallowed; repeated acceptance requests can repeatedly invoke the award helper.
Verification, EXP award, and notification are separate operations with swallowed failures; repeat requests can re-trigger side effects.
The answer count is blindly decremented when soft-deleting, with no demonstrated nonnegative or concurrency-safe transition predicate.

implementationRisks.impact: Retries, concurrent requests, or partial failures can produce duplicate EXP, missing notifications, inconsistent verification effects, or incorrect answer counts despite a successful response.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Implement transition-based, idempotent side effects keyed to the answer and transition, and place coupled database changes in one transaction. Update/delete with predicates that prove the prior state, and emit EXP/notification only when the intended state transition actually occurs.

coverage.assessment: Reviewed POST against KX authentication, explicit-role denial, ICS scope, pre-parse Super User denial, and outbound-AI ordering. Baseline explicit SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN denial remains unimplemented.
Reviewed POST against KX authentication, ICS binding, protected input ordering, institute lookup, and outbound-AI ordering. Baseline role fail-closed behavior remains unimplemented.
Reviewed POST against KX authentication, explicit-role denial, protected input ordering, and outbound-AI effects. Baseline explicit SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN denial remains unimplemented.
Reviewed GET as KX_MOD private analytics, including moderator roles, ICS scope, query scoping, and pre-read denial. Baseline implementation currently applies only general KX eligibility.

Reviewed POST for route actor binding, answer-to-post resolution, question-author authority, course-linked visibility, transaction effects, notifications, and EXP ordering. The revised matrix lacks an operation-specific authority statement and resource-input inventory.

Reviewed DELETE for answer authorship/moderator authority, parent institute/course scope, safe 404 behavior, soft deletion, and answer-count effects. Resource inputs are missing from the matrix and baseline staff authority is overbroad.

Reviewed POST as KX_MOD, including instructor aliases, course assignment, answer/post binding, verification state, EXP, and notification ordering. The operation-specific relationship contract is incomplete.

Reviewed GET and POST for authenticated actor ownership, post visibility, institute/course relationship constraints, anonymous-author serialization, and mutation ordering. The POST resource input is omitted from the matrix; baseline post visibility checks remain incomplete.

Reviewed DELETE for canonical actor, comment/answer/post parent traversal, authorship and moderator authority, course relationship, and safe denial. The parent-post-author right is unresolved in the revised contract.

Reviewed POST for actor binding, schema ordering, canonical parent resolution, lock state, institute/course visibility, anonymous serialization, and creation effects. The matrix omits postId/answerId and does not define dual-parent handling.

limitations: This was a document-only pre-implementation design review using only the supplied sanitized packet. No implementation, runtime, database, transaction, test, fixture, or formal-gate claim was evaluated.

Imported AI, serialization, gamification, and schema implementations were not supplied as assigned source bodies; their internal behavior could not be independently inspected. The review assesses ordering and authorization obligations at the assigned route boundaries only.

No acceptance-criteria catalog with formal AC identifiers was supplied. affectedAC values therefore reference the packet's named policy and architecture contracts rather than inventing external requirement IDs.

Operational approver, manifest maintainer/release reviewer, production dataset identity/fingerprint and attestation procedure, expiry lifetime owner, and revocation publication/runbook owner remain unassigned. Their absence blocks production oversight disclosure but does not prevent evaluation of these legacy KX route designs.
